sections.title: A small engine that earns its place
sections.body:
The Habitat Engine should turn a development request into a bounded, observable piece of work: choose an eligible execution recipe, assign an agent, run it in an appropriate workspace, check the result, and retain enough state to recover. It should also tell the operator which services exist, who owns their lifecycle, and whether they are useful now.

The recommendation is **a new, small composition layer**, drawing selectively from the existing projects. HEE-v2 is a component reference, not the default implementation base. Its completion programme is not adopted wholesale. The design deliberately uses ordinary code for coordination and existing runtimes for model interaction and process management.

The proposed v3 product is a modular Rust coordinator, a Julia numerical-analysis package, one SQLite database, human-readable configuration, a CLI, and two worker adapters. Herdr supplies the visible workspace. Pi is the leading candidate for general model-backed workers; an existing native coding harness supplies the second adapter. systemd owns long-running processes. An API gateway is optional and replaceable. The four requested capabilities are the centre of the product, not contingent on a later learning or cognition system.

“Any LLM” means an open adapter contract that can register supported models, including local and remote inference, with explicit capability limits. It cannot mean that every model supports every task or that all proprietary harnesses accept arbitrary models. “Best” means the best supported choice for this task, budget, privacy requirement, toolset and current evidence. It is an explainable decision under constraints, not a permanent global ranking.

Success is practical: a task survives a coordinator restart without a duplicate edit; a worker can be cancelled; a service with a live PID but a stalled request path is reported accurately; and cost per accepted result improves against a fixed-model baseline. A quiet engine incurs no model calls. A routing decision normally incurs no model calls.

This is a researched production engineering plan, not a claim of production readiness. All proposed tasks start idle. The user requested vision and planning, and explicitly redirected the review toward best components and lower complexity. No engine implementation, service activation or provider-integration tests were performed. Three specialist planning reviews were explicitly authorised later in the session. The original SSD home partition was mounted read-only for source research, with journal replay disabled.

sections.title: Component decisions across the local projects
sections.body:
### Firstmate: operational patterns with a real integration surface

Firstmate is an agent distribution: instructions, skills and scripts that arrange visible crews, isolate worktrees, watch events and deliver outcomes. Its most relevant contribution is the split between inexpensive supervision and occasional LLM judgment. The watcher classifies routine events in shell and batches actionable wakes. Requested profiles carry harness, model and effort; profile selection is performed by an agent, not a measured task-quality optimiser. [Architecture](sources/D18.md), [watcher](sources/H12.sh), [spawn](sources/H13.sh).

Adopt the **patterns**: stable task identities, explicit worktree ownership, event cursors, deduplicated notifications, semantic busy state, incarnation binding, and startup reconciliation. The Herdr backend already considers subscription gaps and polling fallback. Its process classifier avoids equating an idle shell with a living agent. These are stronger inputs than terminal-title matching. [Herdr integration](sources/D19.md), [process classifier](sources/H11.sh).

Do not make the entire Firstmate distribution a mandatory dependency. Its supervisor, primary-agent hooks, secondmates, remote homes, self-update and delivery flows are a considerable operational surface. The useful watcher is not evidence that the entire distribution has zero token cost. Let Firstmate remain an optional human-facing client or delegated worker owner. For each task, exactly one system owns dispatch: either Firstmate operates it independently, or the Habitat coordinator owns it and Firstmate submits/observes through an adapter. Never run two retry loops over the same work.

Direct source reuse is possible to assess under its MIT licence, with attribution retained. Before importing a helper, identify its called scripts, environment conventions and state files. If that closure drags in the whole distribution, implement the small behaviour behind a tested adapter instead. There is no benefit in hiding a large dependency tree behind a short wrapper.

### Upstream Pi: reuse the agent runtime

Pi's upstream repository now resolves to `earendil-works/pi`; the inspected manifest uses `@earendil-works/pi-ai` 0.85.1. Older local documentation names earlier packages. Pin an actually tested package/release pair before implementation; do not mix snippets across these generations. The AI layer includes provider collections, usage/cost reporting and context conversion, while agent-core supplies the tool loop and event stream. Its documented model catalogue focuses on tool-calling models. [AI package](sources/A09.md), [agent core](sources/A10.md), [manifest](sources/A13.json).

For a Rust coordinator, use Pi's JSONL RPC subprocess interface. It exposes configured-model discovery, explicit model selection, state queries, usage statistics, retry configuration, abort and streaming events. At this inspected version, `agent_end` can precede automatic retry; `agent_settled` reports the end of the session-level run. Neither proves the task's acceptance criteria. Use the settled event plus artifact verification. LF-only framing and request IDs belong in adapter tests. [RPC contract](sources/A11.md), [RPC implementation](sources/A12.ts).

The product codebase is Rust and Julia, as explicitly required by the user. Pi remains an external worker dependency reached through its documented process interface; its TypeScript implementation does not make TypeScript part of the owned coordinator. Pi session storage is conversation history; the Rust ledger is task ownership and accounting. Link the two by ID rather than copying every message.

Pi is not a universal solution for non-tool models, arbitrary native harnesses, service inventory or task scheduling. Keep a plain inference adapter for models that only return outputs and native harness adapters for workflows whose behaviour depends on their own CLI. Do not rebuild Pi's provider SDKs or agent loop inside the coordinator.

### Herdr Workflow Engine and the Zellij workflow lineage

The migrated workflow lineage contributes versioned templates, stable DAG planning, explicit dependencies and reusable procedures. The current HWE source has a concrete SQLite journal: transactions, idempotency keys, prior-sequence checks and terminal-state checks. It also has a disarmed executor with capsule and receipt mechanisms. The README's older G1/G2 description is therefore incomplete as a current source map, but there is still no live executor. [HWE architecture](sources/A02.md), [SQLite journal](sources/A03.rs), [disarmed executor](sources/A05.rs).

Take the simple parts first: an ordered list of steps, optional dependencies, typed argv, explicit cwd/env, bounded execution and a transaction that rejects conflicting retries. Add general DAG scheduling only when a second real workflow needs it. A first task should not require template mining, a workflow grammar, a signed capsule chain and a separate executor project.

SQLite is the preferred ledger for the new engine. Reuse reviewed ideas from HWE's journal, not its whole migration/admission framework by default. Its path check in the inspected runner is lexical; lexical containment alone is not a sandbox against symlinks or arbitrary commands. Filesystem access must be enforced at the worker boundary. [Dispatch seam](sources/A06.rs).

The Zellij-to-Herdr translation atlas provides a useful durable lesson: pane identity, task identity, service ownership and completion are different things. Preserve that separation even while simplifying the implementation. The loop-engine-v3 archive explicitly describes most of its broader topology as scaffolding; module count is not evidence of useful runtime coverage. [Translation atlas](sources/D17.md), [loop status](sources/H08.rs), [workflow origins](sources/H07.md).

### ORAC-SIDECAR: observation and operational feedback

ORAC contributes event observation, health/circuit-breaker ideas, workspace affinity and historical operating failures. Its semantic router combines task/tool domains, affinity and coupling to choose a pane. This is useful as a locality hint when several eligible workers exist; it is not a demonstrated selector of the best LLM. Unknown tool labels must not inherit permissive authority from a default classification. [Router](sources/H01.rs), [circuit breaker](sources/H02.rs).

The strongest reusable assets are its failure cases. A historical dark-wire record identifies a completion handler that dispatch did not call. An async-starvation RCA describes a process and auxiliary endpoint remaining alive while the main runtime stopped responding. Turn those into tests: request accepted but no completion event; handler registered but never reached; PID alive while useful work stalls; locks or blocking I/O preventing cancellation. The archived handler's local lack of an auth check is a narrow code observation, not proof about all middleware. [Dispatch incident](sources/D15.md), [starvation incident](sources/H05.md).

Keep learned affinity advisory and experimentally bounded. Do not put Kuramoto synchronisation, STDP, emergence scores or a 12-axis fitness tensor in the initial control path. ORAC's own fitness commentary records incentives that needed rebalancing. Task acceptance, elapsed work and measured cost are more direct starting signals than a synthetic health of the whole field. Safety and privacy constraints are eligibility conditions, never small weighted terms. [Fitness implementation](sources/H03.rs).

### HEE-v1, HEE-v2 and the local Pi Harness Engine

HEE-v1 offers a useful observatory/companion boundary and scoped evidence/admission ideas. Its separate recorded microVM work should not be flattened into a claim that everything is inert. Equally, recorded qualification of one slice does not supply a general dispatcher. [HEE-v1 README](sources/D12.md).

HEE-v2 contains substantive code: roster contracts, bounded budgets, durable state, authenticated channels, safe-idle logic and an optional verification worker. Its current joined effect executor is still Shadow. Its model eligibility checks are narrower than the user's desired engine; fit and health scores arrive from callers, and the cost heuristic is not a task-level cost estimator. These are component findings, not grounds to inherit the whole workspace. [Roster](sources/C01.rs), [eligibility](sources/C05.rs), [routing](sources/C04.rs), [cost](sources/C08.rs), [join](sources/A15.rs).

Retain the minimum invariants: recorded task identity, explicit budget arithmetic, distinction between unknown and healthy, cancellation, recovery and acceptance separate from worker claims. Reconsider their implementation for a single-user local coordinator. A custom hash-chained event store, local mTLS infrastructure, autonomous learning programme and 46 closure packets are not prerequisites for that first product. Julia is included by user requirement, with a focused numerical and evaluation role rather than wholesale inheritance of HEE's verification programme. Additional HEE mechanisms remain candidates where a demonstrated requirement justifies them. Existing HEE decisions and evidence stay intact in their own project.

The local Pi Harness Engine likewise has useful bounded request and process-runner work, but explicitly lacks a roster database and Pi runtime integration. It is another source of small components, not a shortcut to an already working engine. Its current review licence blocker is local to that project; this report does not turn it into a universal planning or implementation stop. [Current README](sources/A07.md), [contracts](sources/A08.rs).

sections.title: Swarm orchestration and cohesion: what the Zellij habitat teaches
sections.body:
The Zellij habitat had several overlapping coordination mechanisms rather than one uniformly closed swarm engine. Its historical architecture placed durable objectives in Hermes Kanban/shared-context, tiny signals in Atuin KV, events in Pane-Vortex, policy and intent in ORAC, and verification in a Watcher/Command role. Zellij panes embodied execution. Later plugin pipes reduced dependence on focus-relative keystrokes. These are dated observations and design records, not assertions that those services run on the current Fedora host. [Armada map](sources/S07.md), [communication hierarchy](sources/S03.md), [baton architecture](sources/S18.md).

### Mechanisms worth keeping

| Mechanism | Evidence in the old habitat | Stronger form for this engine |
|---|---|---|
| Role decomposition | Command-1 frames, Command-2 binds work/resources, Command-3 verifies; ALPHA/BETA/GAMMA specialist wings | Named responsibilities and artifacts; one task owner; specialist roles only when useful |
| Durable baton | Write shared-context packet before sending a short pointer | Versioned brief and artifact ID; small per-role context; durable outbox |
| Delivery stages | Queued prompt, receipt/ack, activity, completion and verification are different facts | Explicit per-attempt state transitions with generation-bound acknowledgements |
| Conflict avoidance | ORAC intent tokens, TTL, task mapper and load limits | Transactional resource claims for workspaces/files/services, with fencing |
| Shared awareness | Blackboard, bus events, capability traces and epistemic broadcasts | A bounded task/event view with provenance; material deltas delivered to relevant peers |
| Iterative synthesis | RALPH generations combine specialist results and refine work | Bounded critique/revision on actual failed acceptance criteria, with a stop rule |
| Cohesion signals | Kuramoto phases, coupling weights, STDP and field measurements | Experimental explanatory signals, evaluated against real coordination outcomes |

The original SSD's wiring map is unusually valuable: it records services that were up while particular producer-to-consumer paths carried no useful signal. Fleet dispatches existed while the completion-file path was empty. The new ledger should trace `submitted → acknowledged → executed → artifact → checked → accepted`, and separately record which observer consumed each event. A healthy endpoint cannot stand in for that path. [SSD wiring map](sources/S01.md).

The reliable-fleet design also records that some swarm reviewers cited receiver scripts and line numbers that did not exist. It proposed durable pull delivery to replace focus-relative injection, a good direction, but its proposed `seen-gen`-before-injection ordering could lose work across a crash, and its local hash is not unforgeable authority. Take the addressing and replay lessons; replace the proposed non-transactional KV protocol with SQLite ownership and explicit ambiguous-delivery recovery. [Fleet review](sources/S02.md).

The original `orac-drain` script shows a concrete bridge from ORAC routing decisions into cooperative taskboard work and optional dispatch. Its enqueue path and completion are distinct. This supports the dark-wire diagnosis as a historical integration concern; it does not establish the current state of a deployed drain. [SSD drain script](sources/S04.txt).

### What the inspected code actually does

ORAC's A2A module implements proposed/accepted/in-progress/terminal transitions and bounded history. The task graph provides dependency ordering, and the task mapper considers capability, available load and phase alignment. These modules are behind the `agentic` feature, which is absent from the inspected default feature list. Presence in source is therefore not proof of their historical activation. [A2A](sources/S09.rs), [task graph](sources/S11.rs), [mapper](sources/S12.rs), [features](sources/S16.toml), [module wiring](sources/S17.rs).

The intent bus's inspected conflict query matches the same pane and intent type. That does not prevent two different panes editing the same file. A production swarm needs resource identity and access mode—such as workspace-exclusive or artifact-read—not merely intent labels or phase windows. Resource claims must be checked at the actual effect boundary. [Intent bus](sources/S10.rs).

The swarm-orchestrator plugin is a separate loop from ORAC's RALPH implementation. It starts architect/implementer/tester personas using `claude -p`, combines their output, asks an analyst for a quality score and refined task, and repeats until a score threshold or generation limit. The callback path is event-driven, but each generation includes worker and analyst model calls. It is not token-free supervision. [Plugin source](sources/S15.rs).

Several inspected shortcuts should become regression cases: a worker can be marked done when exit is nonzero but output is non-empty; analysis parse failure assigns quality 0.5; reaching the generation limit enters the same broad complete phase as reaching the quality target; and the shown worker callback does not validate the generation string included at dispatch. These observations concern this captured source, not every later version. The new adapter must reject stale-generation results, keep error output separate, distinguish budget exhaustion from acceptance, and never replace an unreadable evaluation with a success-like score. Prompt payloads should travel through stdin/data framing instead of being interpolated into a shell here-document.

### Cohesion as a measurable engineering property

Operational cohesion means agents work toward the same accepted objective while retaining enough independence to detect errors. Track coverage of assigned subproblems, duplicated work, stale-context use, conflicting writes, handoff delay, unresolved disagreement, integration failures and accepted output per total cost. High agreement alone is not success; three agents can agree on the same false premise.

Use a small cohort: a coordinator assigns bounded tasks, specialists work on non-overlapping ownership, and a checker evaluates the actual assembled artifact. Start with one worker for ordinary tasks. Add parallel specialists when decomposition permits independent useful work. Peer messages carry new evidence or a specific request; avoid all-to-all transcript broadcast. An integrator owns cross-cutting changes, the assembled candidate and integration evidence. Only the coordinator commits acceptance. A shared contract/version prevents each agent solving a different interpretation.

Keep independent initial assessments before sharing opinions on high-consequence questions, preserve dissent and counter-evidence, and resolve disagreements through source or executable checks where possible. A model-family change may reduce some shared errors but is not proof of independence. Do not appoint another model to agree with the first merely to manufacture confidence.

ORAC's coupling code numerically evolves phases and weights; its order parameter measures oscillator alignment. Hash-seeded frequency diversity and learned edge weights are simulation variables. Their relationship to semantic agreement or coding quality must be established, not assumed. Julia can replay those signals alongside task outcomes, test whether they predict coordination failures, and compare a graph-aware policy with simple load/affinity rules. Do not maximise global synchrony: useful specialist diversity and deliberate review disagreement can lower apparent synchrony while improving results. [Coupling](sources/S13.rs), [STDP](sources/S14.rs).

An older anti-idle doctrine kept allocated agents busy with standby audit work. Preserve it only for an explicitly budgeted campaign with useful remaining tasks. The default engine should become quiet when work is done or blocked. Utilisation is not an objective independent of accepted output and cost. [Historical triad loop](sources/S08.md).

sections.title: Orchestrator and specialist agent threads
sections.body:
The implementation campaign uses an **orchestrator agent with specialised, resumable threads**. The orchestrator reasons about decomposition, proposes assignments, resolves interface questions and requests repairs. The Rust coordinator enforces admission, dependencies, ownership, budgets and acceptance. These are different responsibilities: a persuasive orchestrator message cannot grant permissions or close a task. During development, the available Codex orchestration surface can coordinate the build; it is not evidence that the engine's future thread runtime already exists.

A logical thread is a durable specialist work stream: `thread_id`, root/cohort task, role/profile, brief revision, message cursor, checkpoint, current obligation and outcome references. Its small state can be open, waiting or closed; activity is derived from attempts. Initially permit one active attempt per thread. An agent instance/process executes an attempt; a worker session stores conversation; a Herdr pane presents it. A Rust OS thread or async task is a separate implementation detail. Restarting a conversation or reopening a pane never restores authority by itself.

| Specialist thread | Owned contribution | Proposed tasks and handoff |
|---|---|---|
| Orchestrator / integration | Vertical slices, interface decisions, dependency plan, assembled candidate | T01, T06, T20, T22; integrates candidate artifacts and requests checking |
| Rust core and storage | Task state, rosters, reservations, route policy, SQLite | T04, T05, T09, T10; schema/API contract and migration evidence |
| Runtime, concurrency and tool interfaces | Pi/native/inference adapters, cancellation, restart, bounded delivery and integration packages | T02, T03, T07, T08, T11, T22, T28, T29; process and event-sequence evidence |
| Julia and numerical | Rust–Julia exchange, routing/cohort evaluation, optional operators | T12, T21, optional T23/T24; reproducible datasets and quantitative reports |
| Habitat platform | Service roster, systemd/Podman, isolation, Herdr interface | T13–T16; supported host/runtime contract and operational observations |
| Quality / verification | Formatting, pedantic Clippy, tests, fault cases and completion evidence | T25, T17; checks actual integrated candidates and challenges false-green results |
| Security | Threat model, boundary review, defensive tests, finding closure | T26, T27, with reviews of T07/T10/T15/T18; Daybreak Blue profile where available |
| Release / operations | Packaging, provenance, restore/rollback and full-stack pilot | T18–T20; evidence bound to the artifact actually installed |

These are reusable responsibilities, not a fixed fleet of eight always-running agents. Allocate concurrent threads only when dependencies are satisfied, work is separable, and remaining budget/resources support them. A person or one agent can cover several roles on a small slice; consequential checking should use a distinct evidence path. The orchestrator wakes for decisions and material changes, not routine telemetry. No recursive spawning beyond the admitted campaign's bounds.

Each assignment carries the versioned objective, exact artifact/write ownership, interface expectations, allowed tools, acceptance criteria, bounded context and budget, required evidence and next handoff. Shared manifests, lockfiles and cross-language schemas have a named owner. Give each attempt a separate writable workspace and build-output scope; one integrator owns the integration workspace. Acquire multi-resource claims atomically or in a fixed order. Workers return candidate references; they do not concurrently merge into the integration tree.

Thread mailboxes reuse SQLite events/outbox. A message records its identity, sender/recipient, relevant generation, brief revision, artifact references and concrete requested action. Delivery, receipt and action completion are separate. A receipt cannot erase an outstanding obligation across a crash. Bound mailbox/context sizes, coalesce routine progress and preserve cancellation, failures and dissent. Handoffs contain the current contract, decisive evidence, unresolved issues and next action; complete transcripts remain referenced rather than broadcast.

For every vertical slice: the interface owner settles the narrow contract; implementers produce isolated candidates and local check evidence; the integrator assembles them; the verification and security threads check the relevant boundaries; failed criteria return a focused repair task; the coordinator closes only after evidence satisfies the parent contract. Child success is an input to the parent join, not parent completion. Before closure, settle or cancel remaining mutating attempts and prevent late callbacks or writers from changing the verified subject.

Recovery cases include orchestrator loss during decomposition, duplicated child dispatch, obsolete briefs, a crash after mailbox receipt, cancellation during integration, and individually passing children whose combination fails. The future engine must reconstruct the unresolved obligation from its ledger. This makes thread synergy an observable integration property rather than the number of active conversations.

sections.title: External options and complete assembly choices
sections.body:
The external tools solve different layers. The following assessment is an architectural judgment based on source/documentation, not a performance benchmark.

| Option | Useful contribution | Limitation for this engine | Recommended place |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pi AI / agent / coding runtime | Model/provider access, tool loop, structured sessions | Not a service roster or durable fleet scheduler; capability coverage varies | Primary worker candidate |
| Firstmate | Visible crews, worktrees, event supervision | Agent-directed coordination and a broad script closure | Optional operator client; selective patterns |
| LiteLLM | Multi-provider gateway, retries, cooldowns, deployment balancing | More service/configuration to operate; balancing is not coding-quality selection | Optional gateway when several consumers need it |
| Bifrost | Go gateway with unified API, provider failover and management surface | Edition boundaries matter; vendor speed claims are not local measurements | Gateway contender alongside LiteLLM |
| OpenRouter | Managed access and model/provider routing | External dependency; automatic choice is not a Habitat acceptance score | Optional provider route or evaluation baseline |
| RouteLLM | Learned cost/quality routing methodology | Training/evaluation work; published task distribution differs from ours | Later experiment, not first dependency |
| OpenHands SDK | Coding-oriented agent runtime and tool/server interfaces | Another runtime to qualify and operate | Alternative worker if it beats Pi/native harnesses on local tasks |
| LangGraph | Durable stateful workflows, interrupts, deterministic/agentic steps | Adds a graph runtime and its state semantics | Reconsider if complex long-lived workflows dominate |

LiteLLM's documented routing includes deployment balancing, cooldowns, timeouts and retries. That could save adapter work when many clients share providers; it does not establish which model produces an acceptable patch. Start without a gateway when Pi and native harnesses already cover the selected providers. [LiteLLM routing](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/routing).

Bifrost is a credible gateway alternative, but its current project documentation distinguishes enterprise adaptive balancing and clustering. Compare the specific available edition, streaming fidelity, effective model identity and operational cost. Do not choose on a vendor headline such as a speed multiplier: workstation request volume and model latency may make that difference immaterial. [Bifrost project](https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost), [provider routing](https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/dev/docs/providers/provider-routing.mdx).

OpenRouter's current Auto Router documents task classification followed by rankings based on recent aggregate spend share. That is a useful external prior, not verified quality on this user's repositories. Its documentation also warns that a mismatched plugin ID can silently ignore per-request settings. Explicit allowlists and effective model readback are therefore essential if this route is used. [Auto Router](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/routers/auto-router).

RouteLLM provides evidence that learned preference-based routing can improve a cost/quality tradeoff on evaluated workloads. Use its approach as a later challenger to a cheap deterministic baseline; reproduce the relevant benefit on Habitat tasks before adopting training infrastructure. [RouteLLM paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18665).

OpenHands provides coding-oriented Python/REST APIs and reusable tools; it deserves a controlled worker comparison when coding performance is the limiting factor. LangGraph provides persistence and long-running workflow primitives and can be used without the full LangChain product stack. Either may avoid bespoke work for the right workload, but installing both would introduce overlapping runtime responsibilities. [OpenHands SDK](https://docs.openhands.dev/sdk), [LangGraph overview](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/overview).

### Assembly choices under the Rust and Julia requirement

| Assembly | Benefits | Costs and failure modes | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Firstmate + provider access + a small service inventory | Fast route to visible crew work; little new scheduling code | Core coordination depends on the liaison agent; bespoke quality/cost ledger still needed | Useful operational baseline and quickest trial |
| Rust coordinator + Julia analysis + SQLite + Pi/native workers + systemd | Stable task ownership, quantitative evaluation, replaceable runtimes, little new provider code | Must test process/serialization seams and a small scheduler | Recommended foundation |
| Rust coordinator + Julia analysis + OpenHands/native workers | Preserves the required languages with a different execution ecosystem | Different runtime and interface to qualify | Alternative if Pi underperforms on the actual tasks |

A fourth possibility is extending all of HEE-v2. It has more existing policy machinery, but also imports a large assurance and integration programme that does not directly deliver the four requested capabilities. Given the user's explicit concern, it is not the recommended default. A full ORAC revival similarly imports experimental control mechanisms ahead of demonstrated need.

The first future implementation experiment should qualify the Rust-to-worker seam and Rust-to-Julia data contract, not reopen the language choice. Keep runtime libraries outside the coordinator, and select the worker implementation using actual completion, cancellation, cost and compatibility evidence. No implementation experiment is authorised by this planning request.

sections.title: Proposed architecture and responsibility boundaries
sections.body:
One executable, provisionally `habitat-engine`, exposes CLI subcommands and a `serve` mode. One local service owns scheduling and writes the task ledger. Start with one Rust package containing focused modules and one Julia project for numerical analysis; split further only for an actual independent consumer or release boundary. No public HTTP API, cluster manager, custom message bus or mandatory gateway is needed for the first workstation release.

| Module | Owns | Delegates |
|---|---|---|
| `task` | Task specification, attempts, state transitions, acceptance references | Agent reasoning and repository-specific checks |
| `store` | SQLite transactions, migrations, event/outbox records, query views | Conversation storage to the worker runtime |
| `roster` | Models, agent profiles/instances, services and freshness | Provider discovery and OS observations to adapters |
| `route` | Hard eligibility, profile ranking, fallback plan and explanation | Model transport and inference |
| `budget` | Task reservations, attempt ceilings, usage reconciliation | Provider metering, marked estimated when incomplete |
| `worker` | Common spawn/observe/cancel/result contract | Pi RPC, native CLI or plain inference adapter |
| `service` | Desired state, dependency checks, observed useful health | Process lifecycle to systemd / Podman |
| `herdr` | Task-to-pane mapping and operator actions | Terminal/session implementation to Herdr |
| Julia project | Outcome statistics, routing comparisons, numerical experiments | Admission and policy promotion to Rust |

The stateful core depends on these small ports, not on terminal text, a particular model SDK or vendor dashboard. The public contract can begin as versioned JSON over a private Unix socket plus CLI output. Worker protocols may be Pi RPC, native structured output or a negotiated standard; they need not all masquerade as the same protocol internally.

ACP offers capability/version negotiation for agent-client communication. Use it where a selected harness implements the required version; absence of an optional capability must not become assumed support. MCP is useful for tools/resources offered to an agent, not for owning task leases or service lifecycle. [ACP initialization](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/initialization), [MCP architecture](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/architecture).

The operator may use a Firstmate-style liaison, but it submits the same task specification as the CLI. It cannot manufacture a successful result by saying “done.” The engine presents a small task card: purpose, chosen worker/model, workspace, status, spend, blocking reason and result. Detailed logs and route evidence are drill-down views.

The first workflow is intentionally short: submit → choose → run → check → report. Build dependencies are optional task-to-task edges. Reusable workflow templates can later describe a validated sequence; they should not introduce a second scheduler.

sections.title: Maintainable modules, contextual flow and synergy clusters
sections.body:
Modularity means cohesive responsibilities, narrow interfaces and controlled change propagation. Keep the Rust modules in one package, Julia in one project, and the four thin integration packages at their own documented boundaries. Paths below name responsibility boundaries, not a requirement to generate empty files, one crate per module or a plugin framework. Split a crate only for an actual separate consumer, independently released component or measured build/dependency need. Use private implementation details and typed boundaries; introduce traits at replaceable I/O/worker seams rather than wrapping every helper.

The application composition root wires pure task/routing policies to persistence and runtime adapters. Boundary types are stable and small. Build dependencies point inward; request/result feedback travels through those interfaces. Julia exchanges versioned data through the Rust numerical adapter and is not a Cargo dependency. Dynamic feedback cycles therefore do not require circular module imports. The structured `module_atlas` in the JSON spine includes a proposed acyclic build-dependency graph; it describes the design, not an observed Cargo graph.


| Proposed module | Owns |
|---|---|
| `src/contracts.rs` | Boundary data types, identities, errors and schema versions |
| `src/task.rs` | Task/attempt and bounded verification-loop state |
| `src/store.rs` | SQLite transactions, migrations and outbox persistence |
| `src/roster.rs` | Model, agent, service and observed-capability queries |
| `src/route.rs` | Pure eligibility/ranking and route explanations |
| `src/budget.rs` | Reservation policy and usage reconciliation |
| `src/worker/` | Pi/native/inference process adapters behind the worker contract |
| `src/check.rs` | Protected verifier invocation and criterion evidence |
| `src/recovery.rs` | Attempt reconciliation, ambiguity and cleanup policy |
| `src/cohort.rs` | Logical threads, assignments, resource claims and join obligations |
| `src/context.rs` | Bounded briefs, provenance and artifact-reference selection |
| `src/notify.rs` | Delivery/replay/deduplication of actionable outcomes |
| `src/service.rs` | Useful probes and actions delegated to the registered lifecycle owner |
| `src/herdr.rs` | Herdr client adaptation and task/pane presentation links |
| `src/numerical.rs` | Bounded Rust–Julia process and data boundary |
| `julia/src/HabitatAnalysis.jl` | Evaluation/statistics with internal Evaluate, Cohesion and optional operator submodules |
| `src/main.rs` | CLI/serve composition and dependency injection; no duplicate task state |
| `src/actions.rs` | Authoritative typed action catalogue, capability projection and transport dispatch metadata |
| `integrations/bash/` | Thin shell/Just projection and verdict/argument preservation |
| `integrations/pi/` | Selected versioned Pi bridge, registration/rendering/cancellation |
| `skills/` | Versioned role/task instructions and on-demand references |
| `workflows/` | Finite typed procedure definitions using the existing task/cohort scheduler |

### Synergy clusters

These group cooperating modules; they do not create additional services.

| Cluster | Modules | Cross-codebase contribution | Benefit and check |
|---|---|---|
| K1 · Task ownership and recovery | contracts, task, store, budget, recovery | CB02, CB08, CB03 | One durable ownership/budget/repair authority; crash and duplicate-work failures share one transaction boundary. Restart and competing-attempt schedules preserve ownership, cost and unresolved obligations. |
| K2 · Worker routing and capability | roster, route, worker | CB02, CB09, CB10 | Task-aware policy composes with maintained provider/agent runtimes. Two real adapter types return effective identity, usage, limitations and cancellation. |
| K3 · Thread context and cohesion | cohort, context, notify, skills, workflows | CB04, CB05, CB11 | Durable bounded briefs and actionable feedback connect specialists without transcript broadcast. Obsolete briefs, missing acknowledgements and conflicting ownership cannot masquerade as progress. |
| K4 · Verification and numerical evidence | check, numerical, julia | CB01, CB02, CB05, CB08 | Actual candidate checks and Julia outcome analysis improve choices while preserving separate authority. False completion and misleading numerical reports fail closed against independent fixtures. |
| K5 · Habitat operation and presentation | service, herdr | CB01, CB11, CB12 | Herdr visibility and established lifecycle ownership expose useful state without an LLM status interpreter. Pane reconnect, stalled services and control denial preserve task truth. |
| K6 · Application assembly | app, actions, bash, pi_extension | CB08, CB10, CB11 | One composition root assembles narrow modules; dependency direction remains visible. Packaged full-stack loop reaches accepted completion and delivery with the intended adapters. |

### Bidirectional contextual flow

Requests/results share stable task, attempt, brief and schema identity as applicable. Feedback does not grant authority.

| Flow / boundary | Forward: request and context | Return: result and feedback | Closure check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F01 · herdr → task | Versioned intent and operator constraints enter actions/app; authenticated task-scoped request reaches task | Status, route reason, blocking criterion and completion references | Pane loss does not lose the task; a displayed done message cannot accept it. |
| F02 · task → store | Expected state/generation plus atomic attempt/event changes | Committed identity or typed conflict/storage failure | Crash after commit preserves replayable obligation; same key/different body conflicts. |
| F03 · task → route | Task class, immutable constraints and candidate observations | Eligible recipe, exclusions, evidence freshness and fallback | Ineligible model never dispatches; reverse explanation names every decisive exclusion. |
| F04 · task → roster | Capability/locality/version/health query whose returned facts are passed to pure route policy | Declared and observed facts with identity and age | Missing or stale facts retain unknown status; source refresh does not rewrite history. |
| F05 · task → budget | Attempt/verification reservation and later measured usage | Admit/refuse, remaining budget and reconciliation discrepancy | Concurrent reservations and unknown usage preserve the declared cost mode. |
| F06 · task → worker | Attempt/generation, recipe, owned workspace, limits and cancellation | Ack/activity, usage, candidate references, exit/error and settled state | Every forward dispatch has a reconciled terminal or explicit unknown return; no stale generation acceptance. |
| F07 · task → check | Acceptance revision, immutable candidate and protected fixture references | Criterion observations, checker errors and raw evidence references | Wrong subject, changed fixture, skipped mandatory test or forged pass cannot close. |
| F08 · task → cohort | Parent criteria, child DAG, thread briefs and resource/budget bounds | Child candidates, dissent, integration gaps and join readiness | Successful children cannot bypass the integrated parent check. |
| F09 · cohort → context | Current brief revision, role, permitted sources and context limit | Selected context/artifact pointers, separate source and task-relationship coverage gaps, whole-workflow context cost and provenance | Obsolete briefs and missing decisive context produce explicit rescope, not silent full-corpus reload. |
| F10 · task → notify | Committed outcome event and relevant recipients | Delivery receipt or pending/retryable notification state | Lost notification retries delivery rather than re-executing accepted work. |
| F11 · task → recovery | Persisted active attempts and observed process/session identities | Reconciled state, cleanup result or quarantined ambiguity | Expired lease alone cannot release a live writable workspace. |
| F12 · numerical → julia | Immutable dataset, schema/units, analysis recipe and resource bound | Report/policy candidate, dataset identity, uncertainty and error | Rust validates identity/ranges; Julia cannot write leases, grants or accepted status. |
| F13 · task → numerical | Immutable outcome dataset at declared cutoff, including failed/cancelled/abandoned attempts and unknown usage, plus requested comparison | Validated quantitative report and candidate-policy disposition | A failed or stale analysis leaves the approved baseline unchanged. |
| F14 · roster → service | Explicit discovery, cached-state query or specifically approved bounded probe; lifecycle mutation uses F20 | Timestamped useful-health and actual owner/state observation | A live PID cannot override a failed request-path probe; discovery grants no control. |
| F15 · actions → task | Schema-validated, caller-bound task request and idempotency context | Admission/state/evidence or typed denial/conflict | CLI, Unix API and LLM-tool projections preserve the same authority and effect semantics. |
| F16 · bash → actions | Typed argv/JSON and caller task context | Structured result, decisive exit status and evidence references | Paths/parameters remain literal and presentation cannot swallow a failing producer. |
| F17 · pi_extension → actions | Registered tool call, cancellation signal and admitted versions | Typed result/error, usage, effective identity and evidence | Parallel calls and obsolete reload handlers cannot bypass atomic authority or falsify completion. |
| F18 · skills → context | Selected skill/version, action compatibility and bounded references | Task-scoped instructions, source and relationship provenance, explicit omissions and context preparation cost | Loading instructions grants no effects; stale/incompatible skill references do not silently execute. |
| F19 · workflows → task | Versioned finite action composition and expanded child identity, mediated by actions/app with current authority | Step results, outstanding obligations, repair/stop and parent evidence | Every required child and final verifier contributes to the one parent closure path. |
| F20 · actions → service | Caller-bound explicit grant, registered service/unit/action and durable operation key | Lifecycle owner/job identity, observed result/useful health or unknown effect | Discovery grants no mutation. Lost manager response requires readback; no competing lifecycle owner. |

### Maintainability and drift control

Keep one small module card at the owning source boundary: purpose, public contract, dependencies, owned state, caller/callee links, failure semantics and decisive tests. Derive reverse caller links from the same declared edges instead of hand-maintaining a second diagram. Update the card when a public contract or responsibility changes; ordinary internal refactoring does not require rewriting the atlas.

During consolidation, compare the actual changed surface with its accepted task and contract. Bind check results to the candidate, preserve unresolved findings, and update the same task record. Treat unexpectedly broad change propagation, duplicate state writers, repeated adapter special cases and unrelated module imports as reasons to reconsider a boundary. Measure this on actual changes rather than imposing an arbitrary module-count or lines-of-code target.

A proposal for another crate/service/protocol must name its present consumer, the concrete failure or maintenance cost it removes, alternatives and a removal/migration path. It must not displace required recovery or verification merely to reduce file count. Conversely, a generic abstraction with one speculative consumer should remain a private function or module. Retain the stronger simpler design when evidence supports it, and supersede the old plan entry explicitly.

The consolidation skill is applied here to reconcile planning and scoped conventions. It does not override the user's prohibition on starting engine implementation. Existing source-project standards and completion records are untouched. All proposed engine tasks remain idle; specialist plan reviews are research evidence, not implemented code or deployment proof.

sections.title: API and Unix-socket deployment atlas
sections.body:
### Existing interfaces and what is actually known

| Interface | Owner / caller | Transport and endpoint | Direction and evidence limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Herdr current server | Existing Herdr process; operator clients | Observed Unix socket `/var/home/Louranicas/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`; version 0.9.0, protocol 22 | Read-only status says running/compatible. Captured API schema advertises requests/responses/events; this does not prove every operation was exercised. |
| Firstmate → Herdr | Firstmate backend; Herdr owns endpoint | CLI plus selected raw Unix-socket requests; resolve named session through `herdr session list --json` and match injected `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` | Workspace/pane requests return IDs/state; event subscription feeds watcher decisions. Do not derive a named session path from a mutable label. |
| HEE-v2 channel | HEE-specific authenticated peers | Inspected TLS 1.3 over UnixStream with certificate pins/session binding | Existing protocol is a reference, not the new engine's mandatory channel or a claimed active endpoint. |
| HWE plugin | Herdr invokes a one-shot adapter | argv/environment/JSON invocation; selected architecture uses offline projections | Its captured architecture describes no listening Unix/HTTP/MCP server. Later executor source remains disarmed; no runtime socket is inferred. |
| Pi worker | Coding runtime subprocess; coordinator is parent | LF-delimited JSON over stdin/stdout; stderr diagnostics | Commands return correlated responses and events; `agent_settled` is session-level completion, not acceptance. No Pi Unix listener is required. |
| ORAC / historical Zellij bridges | Historical sidecar, drain, taskboard, KV/plugin-pipe participants | Legacy local hook/API and event/file/pipe mechanisms | Old incident records mention stalled main versus live auxiliary endpoints and incomplete return paths. No ORAC endpoint was activated or assumed live here. |

The current host observation records socket owner UID 1000, socket mode 0600 and parent directory mode 0755; no permissions were changed.

Local evidence: [Herdr API schema](evidence/herdr-api-schema.json), [runtime observation](evidence/host-observation.json), [Firstmate backend](sources/H10.sh), [HEE channel](sources/C17.rs), [HWE boundary](sources/A02.md), [Pi RPC](sources/A11.md), [ORAC incident](sources/H05.md). The saved Herdr schema describes protocol 22 and includes request, success, error, event and subscription-event schemas. Capabilities must be rechecked against the installed pair when implementing.

### Proposed engine endpoints and crossings

| ID / crossing | Listener / lifecycle owner | Transport / discovery | Forward → return | Authority and failure rules |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| API01 Operator → engine | Rust `serve`, started by one user systemd unit | Proposed `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/habitat-engine/control.sock`, private Unix stream | Versioned command → correlated result/error and durable task ID | Private directory/socket, peer and method checks, bounded frames and deadlines; absent/incompatible endpoint is explicit |
| API02 Engine event consumer | Same engine process; separate subscription connection | Same proposed control socket, event subscription operation | Cursor/filter → bounded events, cursor or resync-required response | Persist before publish; slow consumer cannot block task commits; reconnect and snapshot restore current truth |
| API03 Engine → Pi | Per-attempt process owned by worker adapter | stdin/stdout JSONL, selected/pinned executable/package | Set model/prompt/state/abort → response/events/usage/settled | Clear queued work on cancellation; bound framing/output; lost terminal event triggers reconciliation |
| API04 Engine → native / inference runtime | Selected adapter / runtime owner | Version-specific structured subprocess or explicitly configured inference endpoint | Task/inference request → effective identity/output/usage/errors | Declare unsupported capabilities and opaque accounting; no silent transport or privacy fallback |
| API05 Rust → Julia | Bounded analysis process; optional warm worker only after measurement | Versioned file/stdio contract; no default socket daemon | Immutable dataset/reference → typed report/policy candidate | Schema, units, subject, finite values and expiry validated; failure preserves approved policy |
| API06 Engine → Herdr | Existing Herdr server | Discover actual session socket/API capabilities; use public supported interface | Presentation/query/action → IDs/snapshot/events/errors | Engine retains task ownership. Captured Herdr protocol 22 exposes live events, not durable cursors; reconnect/snapshot reconciliation is explicit. No focus-relative dispatch inference. |
| API07 Engine → systemd / Quadlet | Existing user service manager | Explicit systemctl argv initially; D-Bus adapter only if needed | Selected unit action/query → job/state/useful-probe result | Manager owns lifecycle; database state is observed/desired state, not a second supervisor |
| API08 Worker → remote provider / optional gateway | Provider or separately operated gateway | Configured HTTPS; local UDS only if the chosen server actually supports it | Bounded inference/tool request → actual model/provider identity, stream/usage/errors | Task privacy/credentials apply; one retry owner; endpoint allowlist and moving-alias limitations visible |
| API09 Optional numerical service | Julia-native, Rust/LibTorch or external model-service owner | Contract chosen for actual workload; process first, serving endpoint only if justified | Typed field/tensor/domain request → result, reference error and domain/compatibility refusal | Device/artifact identity, shape/units, memory/time and out-of-domain limits required |
| API10 LLM tool channel → action catalogue | Trusted selected worker/tool adapter; same Rust action owner | Native tool channel or optional MCP stdio; no worker-mounted operator socket | Schema-scoped request → same result/error/evidence contract | Caller-bound capabilities revalidated at invocation; tool text cannot grant authority |

API01 is proposed, not installed. No new public HTTP listener, localhost gateway port or per-module Unix socket is required. Use existing OS/runtime interfaces where they already solve the problem. The Rust module boundaries are mostly in-process interfaces; a socket is a deployment and authority boundary, not the default expression of modularity.

### Proposed control contract

Use a small, explicitly versioned LF-delimited JSON request envelope with a request ID, operation and typed parameters; stream events on a separate subscription connection. Publish a JSON Schema for this contract and generate/validate callers against it. This is a new engine protocol, not a claim of wire compatibility with Herdr, Pi, MCP or JSON-RPC. Reject malformed, oversized, unsupported-version and ambiguous requests before effects. Handle split/coalesced stream reads; Unix streams do not preserve application message boundaries.

Initial operation families are: `tools.list/inspect`, `task.preview/submit/get/list/cancel`, operator-only `task.resolve`, `analysis.request/get`, `thread.get/list`, `roster.list/inspect/update/disable`, `service.inspect/probe/action`, `events.subscribe` and `health`. Mutation methods require explicit authorisation and stable idempotency semantics. `task.submit` returns an admitted identity, not an accepted result. The public operator protocol has no worker-callable `task.accept`; internal verification and the coordinator own acceptance. Names are proposed until the Phase-1 contract is fixed.

Replies preserve request identity and either a typed result or a stable error code, retryability and bounded explanation. Include task/attempt generation and event cursor where relevant. Distinguish unsupported, denied, invalid, conflict, unavailable, deadline, budget-exhausted and unknown-effect conditions. Do not turn a timeout into proof that an external operation did not occur. Use explicit query/readback to resolve uncertain effects before replay.

Define frame/output/queue limits, subscription retention and request/probe deadlines in the initial contract and validate their boundary cases. The event API returns resync-required when a cursor predates retention. A request to cancel produces cancellation status; later cleanup confirmation is separate. A disconnected observer does not cancel accepted work unless the task explicitly defines that policy.

### Unix-socket lifecycle and discovery

Resolve the engine runtime directory from the user service environment, with a validated explicit override only where necessary. Create a private owned directory and restrictive socket; verify owner/type and reject ambiguous path substitution. One process owns bind/listen/cleanup. On restart, do not unlink a socket merely because connection failed: establish that it is the expected stale owned endpoint and that another live instance does not own it. Single-instance custody must cover migration and recovery, not just socket bind.

Document socket disappearance on logout/reboot, startup ordering, stale endpoints, permission failures and protocol mismatch. Start with the ordinary user service; socket activation remains an optional packaging decision. Do not enable lingering or expose TCP simply to hide a startup/discovery problem. Toolbx/host and container path views must be verified rather than assuming an identical runtime-directory mount.

For Herdr, retain session/socket/pane identity together. The current default endpoint is an observation, not a path to hardcode for all sessions. Read the actual schema/version, subscribe before reconciling when supported. Captured protocol 22 exposes live events without a durable replay cursor: reconnect and reconcile snapshots; do not promise gap-free historical replay. Durable cursors and resync-required below belong to the proposed engine API02. Do not introduce background API probing on every model token.

Socket permissions separate users, not every process under one UID. Untrusted workers must not receive control mounts or operator capabilities. A local TLS layer may solve a concrete cross-principal identity need, but copying HEE's certificate machinery cannot repair a shared writable home by itself. Qualify stronger user/VM boundaries when the task requires them.

### API completion proof

T02/T03 qualify worker framing and identity; T04/T07 qualify durable request/recovery semantics; T14/T16 qualify service/Herdr adapters; T21 qualifies Julia; T25/T26/T27 qualify checks and security. Each crossing has producer and consumer tests plus an integrated exercise where required. Cover partial writes, duplicate request IDs, slow readers, stale cursors, wrong socket/session, credential denial, process restart and a response lost after the effect. A schema-valid request or a listening socket alone cannot close the path.

sections.title: V3 commands and tool calls that LLMs can discover and use
sections.body:
`herdr-engineering-engine-v3` is now the working project name for this proposed composition engine. No directory with that name was found in the checked home, STORAGE-10TB root or its repos directory. This is a scoped lookup, not a claim that no copy exists elsewhere. The provisional executable remains `habitat-engine`; naming is reversible and does not imply a new project was scaffolded.

An LLM should derive a valid invocation from a **machine-readable action catalogue**, the current task's capabilities and an exact input schema. It should not invent CLI flags or infer executable authority from retrieved notes. One Rust-owned action definition generates the CLI mapping, Unix API schema, selected LLM-tool adapter and reference documentation. The same handler, authorisation and result semantics sit beneath each surface. This prevents three independently maintained interfaces drifting apart.

### Discover → inspect → preview → invoke → observe → verify

Discovery is bounded and filtered by the caller's permitted capability/task scope. It returns action IDs, brief purpose, version and effect class. Inspection returns the selected action's input/output schemas, required capabilities, limits, supported dry-run/readback behaviour and examples. Preview uses current admitted context to report a proposed invocation and exclusions; it grants no authority and starts no worker. Invocation revalidates current authority, catalogue version, task generation and budget. Observation returns actual state and evidence references. Completion remains the verification loop's decision.

An action descriptor includes stable ID/version, owning module, concise semantics, JSON input/output schemas, transport projections, required capability, effect class, credential/egress needs, idempotency policy, timeout/cancellation behaviour, cost mode, readback operation and completion evidence. Dynamic roster availability carries its observation timestamp separately from the stable action schema. A missing action is unsupported; a moving or revoked capability cannot be recovered by guessing a different command.

| Action family | Proposed CLI projection | Proposed LLM-tool projection | Result / closure |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tools.list`, `tools.inspect` | `habitat-engine tools list --json`; `tools inspect <action-id> --json` | `habitat_tools_list`, `habitat_tools_inspect` | Permitted descriptor list or full selected schema; no process/provider activation |
| `task.preview` | `habitat-engine task preview --file <spec.json> --json` | `habitat_task_preview` | Eligibility, planned recipe/argv and known exclusions; does not reserve/dispatch or create permission |
| `task.submit` | `habitat-engine task submit --file <spec.json> --json` | `habitat_task_submit` | Idempotent admission identity and initial state; bounded to the caller's permitted root task/child allocation |
| `task.get`, `task.list` | `habitat-engine task inspect <id> --json`; `task list --json` | `habitat_task_get`, `habitat_task_list` | Actual attempt, loop, cost, blockers and evidence references, subject to visibility scope |
| `task.cancel` | `habitat-engine task cancel <id> --json` | `habitat_task_cancel` | Cancellation requested/observed and separate cleanup state; only the caller's allowed tasks |
| `thread.get`, `thread.list` | `habitat-engine thread inspect <id> --json`; `thread list --json` | `habitat_thread_get`, `habitat_thread_list` | Versioned brief, outstanding obligation, children and handoff state; no transcript broadcast |
| `roster.list`, `roster.inspect` | `habitat-engine roster list --kind <kind> --json`; `roster inspect <id> --json` | `habitat_roster_list`, `habitat_roster_inspect` | Capability, effective/declared identity and freshness; credential references remain filtered metadata |
| `service.probe` | `habitat-engine service probe <id> --json` | `habitat_service_probe` | Bounded approved useful-health observation; probe effects and access are declared |
| `service.action` | `habitat-engine service action <id> <action> --json` | `habitat_service_action`, only for a specifically granted profile | Request to the existing lifecycle owner and state readback; discovery never grants this action |
| `analysis.request`, `analysis.get` | `habitat-engine analysis request --dataset <id> --recipe <id> --json`; `analysis inspect <id> --json` | `habitat_analysis_request`, `habitat_analysis_get` | Bounded Julia work and validated report; no direct route promotion, task acceptance or lease mutation |

These names and argument shapes are proposed contract examples, not installed commands. Generate the final help, schemas and examples from the accepted action definitions. CLI previews expose typed argv arrays and explicit cwd/env metadata with secrets removed; never concatenate model text into a shell command. Do not offer an unrestricted `engine.exec` simply to avoid modelling the few required actions.

### Fit the current worker ecosystem

Select one LLM-facing adapter in the first useful slice: a native harness tool integration or a thin MCP stdio adapter if the chosen harness supports it. Reuse the Rust executable/worker boundary; a standalone tool server daemon is not required. MCP carries tool schemas and results, while the engine retains task ownership and authority. Pi/native agent runtimes keep their existing coding tools; v3 adds the narrow Habitat operations they lack. It does not wrap every compiler, shell command and library in a new proprietary tool protocol.

An untrusted worker must not receive the operator Unix socket to call these tools. A trusted parent/adapter mediates a restricted, task-bound capability projection through its supported tool channel. The engine binds authority to the authenticated caller and active attempt; role names, task IDs and capability claims supplied in model-generated JSON do not grant access. Revalidate at the effect boundary even after filtering discovery. A schema-valid request can still be denied.

Operator-only operations include changing grants, resolving authority-sensitive waits, amending acceptance criteria, promoting routing policy and assigning managed-service ownership. They do not appear in a normal worker's tool catalogue. An orchestrator may propose these changes as data, but cannot approve them for itself. The operator API may expose `task.resolve` for a recorded pending disposition; that operation never manufactures verifier evidence or bypasses unmet criteria.

### Example complete exchange and failure handling

A permitted orchestrator discovers task submission, inspects its schema, constructs a bounded child task with the current parent/brief revision, previews eligibility, then submits with an idempotency key. It retains the returned task ID and observes progress through events or `task.get`. If an acceptance check fails, it receives the concrete criterion and evidence and proposes a repair within the remaining allocation. It reads the final criterion-to-evidence record before reporting accepted completion. An API acknowledgement, tool-call return or worker exit is not that record.

If a connection is lost after submission, use `task.get` with exactly one selector: task ID or submission idempotency key scoped by the authenticated principal and action. The request correlation ID is separate from that durable key. Read back before replay. If the schema changed, refresh the descriptor and reconstruct the call; do not silently coerce arguments. If a tool is denied, surface the reason rather than translating the request into a raw shell workaround. If an event cursor expired, resynchronise the task snapshot. If a model requests a remote route for a local-only task, the same privacy constraint rejects every transport projection.

### Verify discoverability and prevent interface drift

T28 builds the catalogue and one tool adapter. Its acceptance corpus contains real task-shaped requests, omitted/unknown fields, revoked permission, stale catalogue/attempt identity, malicious text in parameters, duplicate submission, truncated result and lost notification. The same admitted action must have equivalent effects and errors through CLI, Unix API and the selected tool adapter. A denied action must stay denied through all three. Compare generated schemas/help with the owning definitions and reject stale projections.

Measure tool-selection success, invalid-call rate, context bytes spent on discovery, repair cost and accepted end-to-end outcomes. Keep common descriptors compact and disclose full schemas only when needed. Add a new action only when an actual workflow needs it; internal module functions and arbitrary shell commands do not automatically become public LLM tools. The catalogue belongs to the same module/API atlas and task ledger, preserving the small-core design.

The Pi base RPC control stream is not an arbitrary engine-tool callback channel. A selected Pi extension needs a separately qualified inherited task-bound pipe pair or maintained native tool bridge. The trusted parent binds caller identity and grants; the worker receives no operator socket. See the schematic IPC04 mapping.

sections.title: Modular Bash, Pi extensions, skills and advanced tool chaining
sections.body:
The additional review admitted 14 selected Toolshed/Pi-vault/upstream-Pi documents. Their useful common architecture is **one owned action/procedure definition, several thin entry points, and explicit result readback**. The source notes contain historical measurements and operating claims; they are not fresh qualification of the installed toolchain. Their declared reverse links are navigation, not reversed execution or permission. [Chaining patterns](sources/B02.md), [runbooks](sources/B08.md), [Pi procedure contracts](sources/B14.md).

### Four small integration packages

| Package boundary | Owns | Delegates to v3 | Update boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bash / Just interface | Argument-safe invocation, useful help/completion and clean machine output | Action semantics, state, retry, budget and verification | Compatible CLI/action schema; independently checked wrapper/source digest |
| Pi extension integration | Tool/command registration, discovery, result rendering and cancellation forwarding | Authorisation, task ownership, completion evidence and durable state | Pinned Pi SDK/runtime + tool schema + extension/bridge identity |
| Skill package | Triggers, compact instructions, examples and on-demand references | Executable semantics and permissions | Content revision, compatible actions and referenced dependency closure |
| Workflow package | A finite declared composition of named actions with typed handoffs | Existing task/cohort scheduler and completion loop | Procedure identity/version, action versions and effect/recovery contract |

These are modular delivery surfaces, not four new control services. The engine's operational and numerical implementation remains Rust and Julia. Bash is a thin requested integration surface. Pi's inspected native extension API uses TypeScript: prefer a maintained bridge to the Rust CLI/API; any custom host-required adapter would be minimal integration glue with its own checks, not a TypeScript engine. Settle that concrete packaging choice before implementing it, while preserving the Rust/Julia core. [Pi extension contract](sources/B10.md).

### Bash designed for composition

Use predictable exit codes, JSON/NDJSON only on stdout in machine mode, and diagnostics/progress on stderr. Preserve underlying failures across logging, filtering and presentation. For a verdict-bearing pipeline, record the decisive producer's exit status as well as the whole pipeline outcome; `set -e` alone is not a complete failure policy. Capture `PIPESTATUS` before another command changes it. A convenient bounded-log wrapper should preserve the actual command's status rather than reporting the success of `tail` or `jq`. The Toolshed guard is documented as advisory and limited to its observed tool surface; it is not a universal security or verification boundary. [Claim-time lessons](sources/B05.md).

Pass argument arrays with explicit cwd/environment, quote paths and literal values, handle spaces/newlines/leading dashes and use null-delimited path transport when filenames are the data. Generate argv from validated actions; never pipe recalled commands, retrieved skills or model output into an interpreter. Interactive pickers select an identity to inspect, not an automatic execution grant. Keep raw terminal/TUI capture separate from structured result collection and bind any reused build result to its actual project/revision.

Just recipes should be thin, inspectable developer entry points into the same Rust checks/actions. Import only reviewed procedure closures. Read an unfamiliar Justfile/runbook as inert source before invoking a preview: the captured installed-runbook analysis says `run --dry-run` still executes preconditions, and content matching alone can accept a nonzero command unless the complete predicate is enforced. V3's own inspection/preview contract must execute no precondition or workload and must not claim compatibility with unsafe legacy semantics. [Runbook limitations](sources/B08.md), [Just notes](sources/B09.md).

Qualify Bash wrappers with `bash -n`, ShellCheck, a selected formatter check such as shfmt, and argument-recording fixtures. Include failing producers behind successful filters, missing input, signal cancellation, output truncation and changed downstream scripts. Use a supported toolchain profile; formatting/lint success does not prove effect safety. [ShellCheck](https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck), [shfmt](https://github.com/mvdan/sh).

### Pi extensions as thin, versioned adapters

At the inspected Pi revision, extensions register LLM tools with `pi.registerTool()` and user commands with `pi.registerCommand()`. Keep the initial tool set small and load additional registered schemas when relevant. The documented additive active-tool mechanism ignores unknown names, so read back the effective tool set rather than assuming discovery activated a requested tool. Pin the actual API/package pair and qualify interactive and headless/RPC behaviour separately. [Pinned extension documentation](sources/B10.md).

Propagate cancellation to every child operation and preserve typed engine status. The inspected API requires tool execution failures to be thrown; returning an object labelled as an error does not set Pi's error flag. Its termination hint only applies when every final result in the current tool batch requests termination; it is not proof of task acceptance. Nested model calls must return their usage where supported, while engine accounting retains declared uncertainty. Do not let a nice tool renderer obscure a failed or partially cancelled action.

Pi's documented parallel tool mode preflights sibling calls sequentially and executes them concurrently; hooks cannot assume they see sibling results. Resource/budget admission must remain atomic in Rust. Extension hooks may block or transform calls/results, so a hook is not evidence independent of the extension runtime. Selected extensions and skills are executable/instruction supply-chain inputs, even when the project has been trusted by the harness.

Keep long-lived resources bounded and close them on session shutdown/reload. Reload can leave code from an old handler running; bind callbacks and tool requests to the admitted extension/session/attempt generation and reject obsolete results. Do not hot-reload a control-affecting extension or mutate an active attempt's effective tool set silently. Reconcile pending calls and settle the boundary before a version switch. Full hot-reload semantics remain a runtime compatibility case, not an architectural assumption.

### Skills with progressive disclosure and explicit authority

Provide concise skill descriptions and only the references needed for the current task. A skill identifies compatible action versions, intended task class, required inputs, effect scope, verification/readback and escalation conditions. Its instructions point to the owning action schema and procedures rather than copying executable policy into every harness. Keep skill content and helper references versioned together; installing or discovering a skill does not authorise its procedures. [Toolshed skill routing](sources/B07.md), [Pi skills](sources/B11.md).

The initial packs should cover habitat inspection, bounded task submission, evidence-driven repair, roster/service inspection, Julia report interpretation and release qualification. They can share reference material while exposing different role-scoped actions. Avoid loading the entire historical corpus or every installed skill into every worker. Test actual discovery/name collisions, selected-skill loading, compatible action lookup and refusal of an out-of-scope instruction.

### Advanced chains with explicit shapes and bounded expansion

The vault distinguishes sequential chains, static DAGs, runtime-discovered trees, matrices and converging webs. Reuse those shapes as workload descriptions only when needed. An initial workflow can remain a finite list of named actions; discovered fan-out expands into the existing task/cohort ledger under the same budget and resource limits. Record the concrete expanded child set, unique stable IDs and join rule. Do not create a second cascade scheduler or equate a declared graph with the expanded executed graph. [Clustering shapes](sources/B03.md).

Shape-aware routing is useful for JSON, diagnostics, diffs, tables and paths, but a superficial shape is only a hint. Prefer an explicit schema/media-type/version from the producer and validate the consumer's requirements. Filled arrays/objects, false/null values, malformed records and empty results all need fixtures; an empty collection alone can conceal a serialization bug. Diagnostic handoffs must include the filename when the consumer needs it. Cross-tool disagreement is a reason to inspect definitions and reference evidence, not to majority-vote a fact. [Shape-directed chaining](sources/B06.md).

Two initial compositions are enough to qualify the surface. A code-quality chain runs admitted build/lint/test actions, retains each verdict, assembles diagnostics against the candidate and closes through the protected verifier. A routing-analysis chain exports immutable attempts, invokes Julia, validates the report and presents a candidate policy for scoped disposition. A review write, service change or other external effect must be read back; the projection's existence cannot prove the underlying outcome. Additional recall, editor and Atuin capture integrations remain bounded clients of these contracts, with recalled text inspected before reuse. [Workflow recipes](sources/B04.md), [Pi/Herdr ownership](sources/B13.md).

### Independently updatable without runtime drift

Each package has an ID, owner, version/digest, compatible engine/action/harness versions, declared inputs/outputs/effects, referenced closure, checks and rollback/removal behaviour. Record its installed and selected versions in the existing artifact/service/profile catalogue; do not add a package-registry daemon. Generated Bash/Just/tool/skill reference projections carry the source identity and are compared with it. Discover additions/removals as well as changed files; a checksum of an incomplete include list cannot detect an omitted new module.

Stage updates, check compatibility and relevant positive/negative cases, then switch the selected profile for new attempts. Active attempts retain their effective module, tool, skill and procedure revisions. A deliberate incompatible switch requires settling/cancelling the affected attempt and a new admitted generation. Reversible configuration/content updates need not rebuild the whole engine; compiled Rust changes follow the normal release path, and database changes use the tested migration/restore policy. No dependency downloads or silent self-update occurs inside an unattended task.

After a public contract changes, regenerate its directly affected projections, test producer and consumer versions, and update the same module/API/task records. Do not rerun unrelated research or create a new status document for each wrapper. This is the consolidation control: one owned meaning, explicit compatibility, narrow updates and truthful completion evidence across all entry points.

### Final Toolshed assimilation

Required source files and task-critical relationships are separate context coverage dimensions. Carry the question, source roles, constraints, missing relationships and unresolved questions; count discovery, supplemental graph reads and repeated context as well as final packet bytes. Reuse unchanged captures where appropriate and narrow the question explicitly when coverage cannot fit. Each Bash/Just/runbook/Pi boundary renders its owned template once and passes literal typed data onward. Keep source additions/removals/changes separate from accepting a new compatibility or source baseline. Exact anchors establish content presence, not behavioral correctness. Installed skills, exposed session skills, tools, MCP servers and plugins remain distinct records; replaceable caches do not own user-authored integrations. See the [ten-note Toolshed review and source ledger](evidence/toolshed-final-context.md).

sections.title: Routing and choosing the best model
sections.body:
Routing has two decisions: **which execution recipe is suitable**, and **which available endpoint should run it**. The recipe includes model/provider identity, harness and version, reasoning effort, tools, context limits, location and resource profile. The same model in two harnesses can produce materially different outcomes.

### Model catalogue
