tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T09 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Capability/context/privacy/availability constraints exclude invalid recipes; rules choose a valid recipe with stable explanation; ties and insufficient evidence use an explicit baseline; routing itself makes zero model calls.

tasks.intent: Account for whole-task cost and bounded fallback
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T10 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Concurrent reservations cannot exceed configured bounds; retries/checking/compaction are included; unknown usage is visible; hard-ceiling tasks reject incompatible accounting; fallback cannot cross privacy or tool constraints.

tasks.intent: Minimise repeated context and noisy supervision
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T11 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Context is bounded to task needs; actionable wakes are deduplicated/batched; controlled idle and repeated unchanged events cause zero model requests; summaries and compaction usage are accounted for. Context records distinguish required source-file coverage from task-critical call/dependency/ownership relationship coverage. Expose each gap and account for discovery, supplemental reads and repeated context as well as final packet size.

tasks.intent: Compare routing against a fixed-model baseline
tasks.route: Julia evaluation engineer + independent task reviewer
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T12 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Held-out representative tasks use the same acceptance method; failed/abandoned attempts enter cost totals; report uncertainty by class and review work. Retain a simple policy unless a challenger improves the declared tradeoff. Julia reports routing and cohort comparisons from the same immutable outcomes, with uncertainty and missingness. Include failed, cancelled and abandoned attempts and unknown usage at an explicit dataset cutoff; disclose exclusion and censoring policy.

tasks.intent: Add bounded cohorts and measurable cohesion
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T22 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Roles share a versioned objective, distinct artifact ownership and bounded messages. Cross-agent resource conflicts and stale-generation callbacks are rejected. Compare one-worker and specialist-cohort outcomes including cost, errors, disagreement and rework; idle cohorts stop. Persist logical thread identity, versioned mailbox obligations and parent join requirements; protect shared interface/lockfile ownership and recover orchestrator loss without duplicate dispatch. Enforce one conserved parent/child allocation tree. Waiting parents release resources children require. Semantic cross-module calls remain mediated by the composition root and current action authority. Thread briefs preserve the task-critical relationships needed by the receiving specialist; a list of included files alone cannot prove adequate context. Narrow the question explicitly when required coverage exceeds its bound.

tasks.intent: Expose one authoritative action catalogue to CLI, API and LLM tools
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T28 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: One action definition drives CLI/Unix schemas and one selected LLM-tool adapter. Bounded discovery/inspection/preview, scoped invocation, identity/idempotency and evidence readback work end to end. Denial remains denial across transports; untrusted workers receive no operator socket; generated projections cannot drift. task.get and analysis.get support their own principal-scoped admission-key readback; service.inspect can query the lifecycle operation key without confusing current health with historic effect. events.subscribe without a cursor provides a bounded coherent bootstrap snapshot plus high-water cursor. Distinguish request correlation from durable idempotency. Base Pi RPC does not supply the engine tool callback path; qualify the actual inherited channel or maintained bridge. Template-produced requests preserve literal typed values at the action boundary; model-emitted risk or approval fields never confer effect authority.

tasks.intent: Build inspect-only service inventory and useful probes
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T13 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Daemon, one-shot, library, remote endpoint and neural-operator records use appropriate observations. Unknown/stale readiness cannot become healthy; discovery claims no lifecycle ownership. Apply T05 admitted-revision and explicit import/export rules to service records. Test service update/disable, restart and stale/invalid import; observed inventory cannot overwrite effective authority or grant lifecycle control.

tasks.intent: Add scoped lifecycle actions through systemd
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T14 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Only explicitly managed units can change state; dependencies and result readback are checked; stalled service, restart loop and coordinator restart cases do not create competing process owners.

tasks.intent: Qualify worker isolation and secret delivery
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T15 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Untrusted worker cannot read coordinator state/socket or unintended credentials; argv/env/cwd are explicit; resource and process-group cleanup are tested; trusted-host mode has an honest separate claim. Qualify isolation for candidate-controlled verification subprocesses, including build.rs, procedural macros, tests and Julia hooks. The trusted launcher/collector remains outside that execution domain; candidate code cannot modify protected fixtures, authoritative evidence, ledger/socket or unrelated secrets.

tasks.intent: Expose the task and roster views in Herdr
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T16 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Task cards show owner, model, state, spend and outcome; pane closure does not erase task state; reconnect resynchronises; event gap/poll fallback and user cancel are exercised on the actual public Herdr API. Display the current loop iteration, failing criterion, remaining budget, completion evidence and notification state. The captured Herdr protocol has live events without durable replay cursors. Qualify resubscription and coherent snapshot reconciliation; do not claim gap-free Herdr history.

tasks.intent: Qualify modular Bash, Pi, skill and workflow integration packages
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T29 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Thin updatable packages share action/procedure identity and preserve authority, arguments, producer exit status, cancellation and evidence. Pi errors/parallel calls/reload and effective tool-set readback are qualified; skills disclose bounded context. Two typed compositions close their real return paths. Version switching preserves active attempts and rollback; no separate scheduler or silent self-update. Keep the admitted package/protocol tuple pinned through every active attempt. Revoked/reloaded tool handlers cannot retain effect authority. No custom Pi-host glue is selected until its concrete packaging need is established. Each integration renders its owned template once, then passes literal typed data rather than copying/re-templating procedure bodies. Focused fixtures include braces, quotes, newlines, dollar signs and leading dashes, with exact final argv/JSON and producer-status checks. Preserve source and relationship coverage with whole-workflow context accounting. Source-change reports cannot advance accepted compatibility/source baselines.

tasks.intent: Exercise the critical failure matrix
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T17 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Lost completion, stalled runtime, stale lease, duplicate submission, exhausted budget, provider failure and disk error each hit the intended boundary. Record exact build/config and limitations; do not substitute test count for outcome. Fabricated done, wrong-subject evidence, mid-check artifact mutation, broken verifier, repeated non-progress, failed parent integration and lost final notification cannot produce false accepted completion. Exercise partial/coalesced frames, slow API readers, stale event cursors, wrong socket/session and lost response after effect. Inject failures between artifact write, durability publication and acceptance commit under the declared filesystem contract. Missing, expired or corrupt evidence at later readback must report current unavailability while preserving the historical event; no fresh verification may be inferred. Fault experiments distinguish invalid fixtures, excluded cells and unmeasured gates. A formatting rejection that prevents the intended behavioral fault does not prove that behavioral detector works.

tasks.intent: Package and prove backup, upgrade and rollback
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T18 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Versioned artifact, dependencies and config are identifiable; login/reboot behaviour is observed; consistent backup restores tasks/artifacts; upgrade and schema-compatible rollback run on disposable state before installation. Before restoring a pre-upgrade database, preserve the failed/current ledger and reconcile post-backup operations, effects and usage. Use a disposable bounded qualification domain; a changed event epoch alone does not prevent replaying external effects erased by restore. Backup/restore and retention must preserve declared durability and unresolved evidence obligations. Retention policy states which accepted proof must remain retrievable; evidence loss is reported rather than silently rewriting acceptance or claiming current proof. Integration freshness reports include source additions/removals/changes; accepting an updated baseline is a separate versioned reconciliation, never an automatic consequence of discovery. Restore qualification compares the expected content/service inventory, includes an omitted-service control and independently reads back answering interfaces and residual processes in the disposable scope. File copying alone cannot prove restored operation; local recovery does not establish off-site disaster recovery.

tasks.intent: Run the constrained real-work pilot
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T19 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Under the concrete commissioning choice D07, run the Phase-1 workload/window; measure accepted work, total cost, rework, idle calls and incidents. Meet declared release targets or fix the observed gap without widening scope. Audit sampled criterion-to-evidence records and real repair loops; report false acceptance, verification error and completion-delivery failures.

tasks.intent: Release the scoped product and prune unnecessary machinery
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T20 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: A fresh operator can submit, inspect, cancel, recover and manage the declared services. Publish supported versions/limits and actual evidence. Remove duplicate status/procedure sources; advanced roadmap items remain optional. Pruning/update review keeps observed drift separate from the accepted baseline. Exact source anchors support presence/location claims only, not runtime behavior or compatibility.

tasks.intent: Close security findings against the integrated release
tasks.route: Security + verification threads, separate from finding implementer
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T27 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Reproduce material findings, verify fixes and residual dispositions on the actual packaged candidate. Prompt injection, credential exposure, socket/method misuse, stale writers, fabricated evidence, dependency drift and resource exhaustion cannot produce false acceptance. Model review alone is not closure. In disposable qualified fixtures, candidate build/test code attempts to alter protected fixture, evidence and control paths. The boundary must refuse the effect and the independent collector must expose the attempt; an exit-zero candidate report cannot certify its own integrity. Security fault cases require a valid unmutated baseline and the intended observable refusal. Preserve unmeasured/excluded scope; one corpus with no unique catch does not justify removing a gate.

tasks.intent: Qualify a PyTorch-compatible numerical worker only when justified
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T23 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Compare Julia-native execution with a selected tch/LibTorch or external model-service path on the same model/data. Record language boundary, versions, device, operator support, memory/copy/startup cost and cancellation. A reject/defer decision is a valid outcome; no mandatory Python product code.

tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T24 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: A defined function/field domain, dataset and decision use case exist. Held-out time/topology/domain tests compare prediction and actual scheduling value against simple baselines, including all resource cost. Out-of-domain detection and fallback are tested; rejection leaves baseline routing unchanged.

flows.return_context: Committed identity or typed conflict/storage failure
flows.closure_check: Crash after commit preserves replayable obligation; same key/different body conflicts.

flows.request_context: Task class, immutable constraints and candidate observations

flows.closure_check: Every forward dispatch has a reconciled terminal or explicit unknown return; no stale generation acceptance.

flows.request_context: Acceptance revision, immutable candidate and protected fixture references
flows.return_context: Criterion observations, checker errors and raw evidence references

flows.request_context: Parent criteria, child DAG, thread briefs and resource/budget bounds
flows.return_context: Child candidates, dissent, integration gaps and join readiness
flows.closure_check: Successful children cannot bypass the integrated parent check.

flows.request_context: Current brief revision, role, permitted sources and context limit
flows.return_context: Selected context/artifact pointers, separate source and task-relationship coverage gaps, whole-workflow context cost and provenance
flows.closure_check: Obsolete briefs and missing decisive context produce explicit rescope, not silent full-corpus reload.

flows.request_context: Committed outcome event and relevant recipients
flows.return_context: Delivery receipt or pending/retryable notification state
flows.closure_check: Lost notification retries delivery rather than re-executing accepted work.

flows.request_context: Persisted active attempts and observed process/session identities
flows.return_context: Reconciled state, cleanup result or quarantined ambiguity
flows.closure_check: Expired lease alone cannot release a live writable workspace.

flows.request_context: Immutable dataset, schema/units, analysis recipe and resource bound

flows.closure_check: Rust validates identity/ranges; Julia cannot write leases, grants or accepted status.

flows.request_context: Immutable outcome dataset at declared cutoff, including failed/cancelled/abandoned attempts and unknown usage, plus requested comparison

flows.request_context: Typed argv/JSON and caller task context

flows.closure_check: Paths/parameters remain literal and presentation cannot swallow a failing producer.

flows.request_context: Registered tool call, cancellation signal and admitted versions

rules: Every public action maps to one typed owner through actions/app. Pure modules consume snapshots; requests in the flow atlas describe semantic cooperation, not imports.
A transport can carry many actions. Internal task.accept, raw database mutation and grant self-escalation have no public worker projection.
CLI argv examples and field descriptions are proposed contracts. They are not installed commands, executable schemas, accepted flags or authorisation to run them.
Command files preserve literal argv, cwd and explicit environment; stdout carries bounded structured results and stderr diagnostics. Output formatting must retain the decisive producer exit code.
Read-only action previews do not run preconditions/probes that have effects. Costly probes and analysis are explicit bounded actions.
Any transport timeout distinguishes request delivery from effect completion. Mutation handlers retain operation identity and a queryable readback path.

Numeric limits are contract parameters to fix in T01/T25, not invented guarantees: request/frame bytes, JSON depth, connections, subscriptions, output, mailbox, retention, deadline and resource maxima. Validate platform socket-path byte limits and establish restrictive modes at creation; clients also validate the expected server endpoint identity.

Process-local deadlines use monotonic timing. Persisted time observations include boot/session identity and conservative recovery rules; reboot, suspend and wall-clock changes cannot resurrect leases or make stale observations current.

The catalogue maps planned capacity, not first-slice implementation scope. T01 fixes only needed initial descriptors; T28/T29 qualify additional surfaces. Grant administration, criteria amendment and route promotion remain reserved operator dispositions with no invented worker tools or new administration subsystem.

An unrelated catalogue revision need not invalidate a compatible unchanged action. Check the selected action contract and current caller authority; pin active attempt/package versions and reject incompatible changes.
Accepted completion remains in the task loop. API success, shell exit zero, Pi settled, manager job success and notification delivery are separate observations.
schematic_atlas.interpretation: Schematics are projections of the planning spine, not observed v3 execution. Source projects retain their recorded evidence limits.

review_changes.subject: Herdr events
review_changes.correction: Captured protocol 22 has live event envelopes without a durable cursor. Keep durable replay in API02; Herdr uses live subscription plus snapshot reconciliation.

review_changes.subject: Lost submission acknowledgement
review_changes.correction: Define task.get with task_id OR principal-scoped idempotency_key. Separate correlation IDs from durable operation keys.

review_changes.subject: First-slice budget
review_changes.correction: Add minimum conservative attempt and verification reservation in T04/T06; T10 extends reconciliation across adapters.

review_changes.subject: Pi engine-tool transport
review_changes.correction: Base Pi RPC does not automatically carry custom engine tool calls. Qualify a separate task-bound inherited bridge; no operator socket in worker.

review_changes.subject: Lifecycle authority
review_changes.correction: Roster discovery/probing does not own service mutation. Add explicit actions-to-service semantic flow with grant and readback.

review_changes.subject: Outcome dataset
review_changes.correction: Analysis includes failures, cancellations, abandonment and uncertain usage at a declared cutoff, not only successful completed tasks.

review_changes.subject: State decomposition
review_changes.correction: Task outcome, attempt execution, effect certainty, cancellation cleanup, verification and delivery are separate dimensions with explicit transition guards.

review_changes.subject: Completion evidence custody
review_changes.correction: Allocate event identity before acceptance; write immutable manifest before transaction reference; keep delivery receipts outside immutable manifest.

review_changes.subject: Compositional authority
review_changes.correction: Herdr/task and workflow/task semantic paths enter the common action boundary. Parent/child budgets conserve one allocation tree and avoid resource deadlock.

review_changes.subject: Update boundaries
review_changes.correction: Independent integration updates require a qualified compatibility tuple. Core private Rust modules ship together; active attempts retain admitted versions.

review_changes.subject: Event bootstrap and mutation readback
review_changes.correction: events.subscribe maps API02 and has an explicit bounded snapshot/cursor bootstrap. Analysis and lifecycle operation keys have scoped readback selectors.

review_changes.subject: Cancellation and live recovery
review_changes.correction: A committed cancellation intent blocks acceptance before terminal cleanup. Startup may reattach a positively reconciled live attempt without cancellation or redispatch.

review_changes.subject: Database restore and external effects
review_changes.correction: Preserve the failed/current ledger and reconcile post-backup operations before re-admission. Cursor epochs alone cannot prevent replay of forgotten effects.

review_changes.subject: Roster revision authority
review_changes.correction: TOML is explicit bootstrap/import/export. SQLite owns admitted record revisions; stale file imports cannot erase updates or re-enable disabled records.

review_changes.subject: Candidate code inside verification
review_changes.correction: Trusted launcher/collector is separate from candidate-controlled build/test execution. Build scripts, procedural macros, tests and Julia hooks receive the qualified isolation boundary.

review_changes.subject: Crash durability and evidence availability
review_changes.correction: Publish evidence under the declared filesystem durability contract before committing ledger references. Preserve historical acceptance while disclosing missing, expired or corrupt evidence at readback.

review_changes.subject: Context relationship coverage
review_changes.correction: Required files and required task relationships are separate coverage dimensions. Count discovery and supplemental reads in total context cost.

review_changes.subject: Template ownership
review_changes.correction: Render each owned template layer once; pass literal typed values across subsequent boundaries and verify final argv/JSON identity.

review_changes.subject: Drift baseline authority
review_changes.correction: Detect added, removed and changed sources without automatically accepting the observed baseline. Exact anchors prove presence, not behavior.

review_changes.subject: Gate discrimination
review_changes.correction: Use a valid baseline and an intended fault; preserve invalid-fixture, excluded and unmeasured status rather than manufacturing a pass.

| unsupported | Unknown action, protocol, capability or required accounting | Select supported contract; no guessed flags |
| denied | Caller lacks current grant or target scope | Surface denial; do not route through raw shell |
| conflict | Version/generation or key/body disagreement | Read back authoritative state before resubmission |
| unavailable | Dependency absent or coordinator not ready | Bounded wait under task policy |
| deadline | Request or operation time bound reached | Read effect state; timeout does not mean no effect |
| budget_exhausted | Allocation or declared accounting ceiling cannot admit work | Stop/refuse or request explicit disposition |
| unknown_effect | External result cannot be established | Quarantine and reconcile; automatic replay prohibited |
| resync_required | Engine event cursor/epoch invalid or expired | Coherent snapshot with high-water cursor, then resume |
| verification_error | Checker failed, wrong subject or invalid evidence | Repair instrument; never treat as candidate PASS |

handbook_sections.title: Complete bidirectional semantic flow mapping
handbook_sections.body:
| Flow | Boundary | Request | Return | Closure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F01 | herdr → task | Versioned intent and operator constraints enter actions/app; authenticated task-scoped request reaches task | Status, route reason, blocking criterion and completion references | Pane loss does not lose the task; a displayed done message cannot accept it. |
| F02 | task → store | Expected state/generation plus atomic attempt/event changes | Committed identity or typed conflict/storage failure | Crash after commit preserves replayable obligation; same key/different body conflicts. |
| F03 | task → route | Task class, immutable constraints and candidate observations | Eligible recipe, exclusions, evidence freshness and fallback | Ineligible model never dispatches; reverse explanation names every decisive exclusion. |
| F04 | task → roster | Capability/locality/version/health query whose returned facts are passed to pure route policy | Declared and observed facts with identity and age | Missing or stale facts retain unknown status; source refresh does not rewrite history. |
| F05 | task → budget | Attempt/verification reservation and later measured usage | Admit/refuse, remaining budget and reconciliation discrepancy | Concurrent reservations and unknown usage preserve the declared cost mode. |
| F06 | task → worker | Attempt/generation, recipe, owned workspace, limits and cancellation | Ack/activity, usage, candidate references, exit/error and settled state | Every forward dispatch has a reconciled terminal or explicit unknown return; no stale generation acceptance. |
| F07 | task → check | Acceptance revision, immutable candidate and protected fixture references | Criterion observations, checker errors and raw evidence references | Wrong subject, changed fixture, skipped mandatory test or forged pass cannot close. |
| F08 | task → cohort | Parent criteria, child DAG, thread briefs and resource/budget bounds | Child candidates, dissent, integration gaps and join readiness | Successful children cannot bypass the integrated parent check. |
| F09 | cohort → context | Current brief revision, role, permitted sources and context limit | Selected context/artifact pointers, separate source and task-relationship coverage gaps, whole-workflow context cost and provenance | Obsolete briefs and missing decisive context produce explicit rescope, not silent full-corpus reload. |
| F10 | task → notify | Committed outcome event and relevant recipients | Delivery receipt or pending/retryable notification state | Lost notification retries delivery rather than re-executing accepted work. |
| F11 | task → recovery | Persisted active attempts and observed process/session identities | Reconciled state, cleanup result or quarantined ambiguity | Expired lease alone cannot release a live writable workspace. |
| F12 | numerical → julia | Immutable dataset, schema/units, analysis recipe and resource bound | Report/policy candidate, dataset identity, uncertainty and error | Rust validates identity/ranges; Julia cannot write leases, grants or accepted status. |
| F13 | task → numerical | Immutable outcome dataset at declared cutoff, including failed/cancelled/abandoned attempts and unknown usage, plus requested comparison | Validated quantitative report and candidate-policy disposition | A failed or stale analysis leaves the approved baseline unchanged. |
| F14 | roster → service | Explicit discovery, cached-state query or specifically approved bounded probe; lifecycle mutation uses F20 | Timestamped useful-health and actual owner/state observation | A live PID cannot override a failed request-path probe; discovery grants no control. |
| F15 | actions → task | Schema-validated, caller-bound task request and idempotency context | Admission/state/evidence or typed denial/conflict | CLI, Unix API and LLM-tool projections preserve the same authority and effect semantics. |
| F16 | bash → actions | Typed argv/JSON and caller task context | Structured result, decisive exit status and evidence references | Paths/parameters remain literal and presentation cannot swallow a failing producer. |
| F17 | pi_extension → actions | Registered tool call, cancellation signal and admitted versions | Typed result/error, usage, effective identity and evidence | Parallel calls and obsolete reload handlers cannot bypass atomic authority or falsify completion. |
| F18 | skills → context | Selected skill/version, action compatibility and bounded references | Task-scoped instructions, source and relationship provenance, explicit omissions and context preparation cost | Loading instructions grants no effects; stale/incompatible skill references do not silently execute. |
| F19 | workflows → task | Versioned finite action composition and expanded child identity, mediated by actions/app with current authority | Step results, outstanding obligations, repair/stop and parent evidence | Every required child and final verifier contributes to the one parent closure path. |
| F20 | actions → service | Caller-bound explicit grant, registered service/unit/action and durable operation key | Lifecycle owner/job identity, observed result/useful health or unknown effect | Discovery grants no mutation. Lost manager response requires readback; no competing lifecycle owner. |

handbook_sections.title: Pinned Pi control commands and the separate tool bridge
handbook_sections.body:
| Intent | Captured Pi command / event | Engine interpretation | Closure / limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Discover/select recipe | get_available_models; set_model; set_thinking_level; get_state | Validate requested versus effective model/provider/effort | Record pinned Pi version; unavailable settings are explicit |
| Start work | prompt -> response; asynchronous session events | Command acknowledgement is separate from execution | One independently attributed root attempt per owned session; events may lack request IDs |
| Observe work | get_state; get_session_stats; agent_settled | Return actual session/activity/usage and candidate references | Settled is not task acceptance; all required engine checks still run |
| Cancel | clear_queue before abort; process-scope cleanup if needed | Stop accepting new tool/child work, clear follow-ups, then abort | Observe cleanup; signal alone does not settle subprocesses or remote effects |
| Inspect host resources | get_commands | Extension/prompt/skill inventory | Not a privileged engine action catalogue |
| Interactive request | extension_ui_request | Record a pending interaction or explicit unsupported/cancel result | No automatic approval inferred from a UI message |
| Custom engine tool | Selected extension/maintained bridge -> IPC04 | Separately qualified inherited task-bound channel | TypeScript extension under worker privileges is not the security authority |

These command names come from the pinned [Pi RPC snapshot](sources/A11.md), with implementation context in [A12](sources/A12.ts) and [extension contract B10](sources/B10.md). No runtime commands were executed by this planning review.

handbook_sections.title: Selective Herdr API mapping and complete advertised inventory
handbook_sections.body:
| Purpose | Advertised methods | Engine use / restriction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Discovery | ping; session.snapshot; workspace.list; pane.get | Validate installed protocol and stable session/pane identity |
| Live observation | events.subscribe; events.wait; pane.read | Live events and state readback only; protect sensitive pane contents |
| Task presentation | pane.report_agent; pane.report_agent_session; pane.report_metadata | Attach only owned source/task identity; seq is ordering, not authentication |
| Notification / layout | notification.show; selected workspace/tab/pane operations | Explicitly scoped presentation; never task acceptance |
| Optional worker adapter | agent.start; agent.prompt; pane.send_text; pane.send_keys; pane.send_input | Alternative qualified execution owner only; do not duplicate the Pi launch path |
| Broad control excluded | server.stop; command.invoke; plugin/install/lifecycle operations | Not automatically imported into the LLM action catalogue |

The [complete 102-method inventory](evidence/herdr-api-summary.json) and [captured protocol 22 schema](evidence/herdr-api-schema.json) are advertised capabilities, not exercised operations. Request uses id/method/params; success uses id/result; errors use id/error; live events use event/data. The response schema is a union, not a per-method operational proof. EventsSubscribeParams has subscriptions and EventsWaitParams has match_event/timeout_ms; neither advertises durable replay. AgentStartParams.timeout_ms has a description stricter than its machine minimum, so semantic boundary tests remain necessary.

handbook_sections.title: Failure propagation, containment and recovery
handbook_sections.body:
| Failure | Affected boundary | Required containment / surviving capacity | Existing tasks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Storage full / commit failure | store and all mutations | Stop admissions/acceptance writes, preserve unknown effect state; expose readiness failure without making false commits | T04, T07, T17 |
| Coordinator crash after launch | worker ownership | Recover persisted intent and process incarnation; no blind replay; isolate/quarantine old workspace | T07, T17 |
| Provider outage / rate limit | selected worker recipe | One bounded retry owner; eligible fallback only under original privacy, tools and budget | T08, T10, T17 |
| Worker output spoof / huge output | worker -> check | Bound parsing/logs; worker success-shaped text cannot supply trusted evidence | T03, T15, T25, T27 |
| Verifier crash or fixture drift | check -> task | Instrument error/invalidated evidence; no automatic artifact pass or blind candidate rewrite | T06, T17, T25 |
| Child success, parent integration fails | cohort -> check | Record integrated counterexample and bounded targeted repair; parent stays unaccepted | T22, T17 |
| Herdr disconnect / closed pane | presentation | Keep task ledger and execution; reconnect/resnapshot; display attachment may be absent | T16, T17 |
| Lost accepted notification | outbox -> client | Retry delivery only using event ID; immutable accepted outcome remains intact | T04, T11, T17 |
| Julia report invalid / analysis unavailable | numerical | Reject report; retain approved deterministic baseline; no grant/lease mutation | T21, T12 |
| Stale extension after reload | IPC04 / actions | Reject obsolete generation/grant before effect; pin active tuple or retire safely | T28, T29, T27 |
| Schema-incompatible update | deployment | Refuse switch or use tested restore; retain evidence and reject stale event epoch | T18, T29 |
| Ambiguous external write | recovery | Read back operation identity; wait for disposition if unresolved; cancellation cannot erase past effects | T07, T17, T27 |
